topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Under Ohio's Boating Education Requirement, a person born on or after January 1, 1982, must complete a certificate before operating a powercraft powered by more than how many horsepower?
choice_c: 25 horsepower
choice_d: 50 horsepower
explanation: No person born on or after January 1, 1982, shall operate a powercraft powered by more than 10 horsepower without a boater education certificate.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Which of the following satisfies Ohio's boating education certificate requirement?
choice_a: Any online quiz about boating safety
choice_b: A NASBLA-approved boating course, or a proficiency examination approved by the ODNR Division of Parks and Watercraft
choice_c: A hunting safety course
choice_d: A valid driver's license issued after 2015
explanation: The certificate must come from either a NASBLA-approved boating course or a proficiency examination approved by the ODNR Division of Parks and Watercraft.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Who is exempt from Ohio's boating education requirement while operating a recreational vessel?
choice_b: Anyone who owns their own boat
choice_c: A person who possesses a valid U.S. Coast Guard merchant mariner credential with at least a master or operator endorsement
choice_d: Anyone who has completed a hunter education course
explanation: A person with a valid merchant mariner credential with at least one endorsement of master or operator is exempt while operating a recreational vessel, but must carry documentation.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: A boater required to have a boating education certificate is stopped by a law enforcement officer. Within how many hours must they present the certificate or proof of holding it?
choice_c: 7 days
choice_d: 72 hours
explanation: A person required to have the certificate must present it, or proof of holding it, to the officer within 72 hours of being stopped.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: A rental business may rent a powercraft over 10 horsepower to a person born on or after January 1, 1982, who has NOT completed a boating course, if the renter instead does what?
choice_a: Receives educational materials and passes an abbreviated exam with a score of 90 percent or better
choice_c: Pays an additional security deposit
choice_d: Presents a valid fishing license
explanation: A renter may instead receive educational materials from the rental business and pass an abbreviated exam with a score of 90 percent or better, noted on the rental agreement.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Under Ohio's Child Operators law, at what minimum age may a person operate a personal watercraft (PWC) if a qualified supervising person 18 or older is also on board?
choice_c: 10 years old
choice_d: 14 years old
explanation: Individuals not less than 12, nor more than 15 years of age, may operate a PWC if a supervising person 18 years of age or older is also on board.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: A person under 12 years of age may operate a general vessel (not a PWC or powercraft over 10hp) only under what condition?
choice_b: Only if wearing a PFD, with no supervision required
choice_c: Under the direct visual and audible supervision of a person 18 years of age or older
choice_d: Only on private lakes
explanation: No person under 12 years of age shall operate any vessel unless under the direct visual and audible supervision of a person who is 18 years of age or older.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: A child operator under age 16 operating a powercraft powered by more than 10 horsepower must meet what requirement, even while supervised by an adult?
choice_a: No additional requirement -- adult supervision is always sufficient
choice_b: A separate youth-only licensing exam not required of adults
choice_c: Written parental consent filed with the Division annually
choice_d: The mandatory boating education requirements under ORC 1547.05
explanation: Child operators operating powercraft powered by more than 10 horsepower are required to meet the mandatory education requirements even while supervised by a person 18 years of age or older.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Under Ohio's PWC law, during what hours is personal watercraft operation prohibited?
choice_c: PWCs may be operated at any hour with lights on
choice_d: Before 9:00 a.m. only
explanation: No person shall operate a personal watercraft between sunset and sunrise.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Which of the following is listed as an example of unsafe/reckless vessel operation under Ohio law?
choice_a: Operating at idle speed near a marina
choice_b: Operating within 200 feet directly behind a person water skiing
choice_c: Displaying navigation lights while underway at night
choice_d: Carrying an anchor with a 10:1 scope
explanation: Unsafe operation includes operating less than two hundred feet directly behind a person water skiing or attempting to water ski.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Becoming airborne while crossing the wake of another vessel is considered unsafe operation if it happens at what distance from the vessel creating the wake?
choice_c: Less than 100 feet, or an otherwise unsafe distance
choice_d: Any distance, this is never considered unsafe
explanation: Unsafe operation includes a vessel becoming airborne while crossing another vessel's wake at a distance of less than one hundred feet, or at an unsafe distance.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Which of the following is listed as an "unsafe condition" a law enforcement officer may order corrected under ORC 1547.071?
choice_a: A boat painted a dull color
choice_b: A boat with an outdated but still valid registration
choice_c: An operator wearing sunglasses at night
choice_d: Insufficient personal flotation devices aboard
explanation: Insufficient personal flotation devices is listed among the unsafe conditions an officer may order corrected, along with insufficient fire extinguishers, overloading, improper lights, fuel leaks, and improper ventilation.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: What is a boat operator's obligation if a law enforcement officer determines an unsafe condition presents an especially hazardous risk?
choice_a: The operator must take immediate, reasonable action to correct the situation, which may include returning to shore
choice_b: The operator may ignore the officer if they disagree with the assessment
choice_c: The operator must pay a fine on the spot before continuing
choice_d: The operator's registration is automatically revoked
explanation: The officer may direct the operator to take immediate, reasonable actions to correct the situation, including returning the vessel to shore until the condition is corrected.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: No person shall operate a vessel at greater than idle speed or create a wake within how many feet of a marina, boat docking facility, or launch ramp on Lake Erie or the Ohio River?
choice_c: 200 feet
choice_d: 500 feet
explanation: No person shall operate a vessel at greater than idle speed or create a wake within 300 feet of any marina, boat docking facility, boat gasoline dock, launch ramp, recreational boat harbor or harbor entrance on Lake Erie or the Ohio River.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: How does Ohio law define "idle speed"?
choice_b: Any speed under 20 miles per hour
choice_c: The slowest possible speed needed to maintain steerage and maneuverability
choice_d: A speed at which the engine is completely off
explanation: "Idle speed" is the slowest possible speed needed to maintain steerage and maneuverability.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: How does Ohio law define a vessel's "wake"?
choice_a: The maximum speed a vessel can achieve
choice_b: The area directly behind a vessel where fishing is prohibited
choice_c: The distance a vessel travels in one hour
choice_d: A track left in the water by a watercraft, causing waves that may cause discomfort, injury, or damage
explanation: "Wake" is defined as a track left in the water by a watercraft, causing waves that may cause discomfort, injury or damage to persons, watercraft or property.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Except in cases of distress, what is prohibited regarding buoys and other aids to navigation?
choice_a: Mooring, anchoring, or tying to any marker, aid, buoy, light or other aid to navigation
choice_c: Reporting a damaged buoy to the Division
choice_d: Passing within 300 feet of a buoy
explanation: Unless in distress, no person shall moor, anchor or tie to any marker, aid, buoy, light or other aid to navigation.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Under Ohio's OUI law, at what Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) is it an offense to operate a vessel, for an operator 21 or older?
choice_c: 0.10 or more
choice_d: 0.15 or more
explanation: It is an offense to operate a vessel while having a BAC of 0.08 or more.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: For a person under 21 years of age, at what BAC is it an offense to operate a vessel?
choice_c: 0.02 or more
choice_d: Any amount of alcohol is legal for a passenger, but never for the operator regardless of BAC
explanation: For persons under 21 years of age, it is an offense to operate a vessel while having a BAC of 0.02 or more.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: What is the minimum jail term for a FIRST OUI offense while operating a vessel in Ohio?
choice_c: 30 days
choice_d: 3 days
explanation: The minimum penalty for a first OUI offense is 3 days in jail and a $150 fine.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: If a person under arrest refuses to submit to a chemical test for alcohol/drugs while operating a vessel, what happens?
choice_a: There is no consequence for refusing
choice_b: The person is prohibited from operating a vessel or registering a vessel for a one-year period
choice_c: The refusal automatically counts as a not-guilty verdict
choice_d: The person must complete a boating course within 30 days instead
explanation: If a person under arrest refuses a chemical test, they are prohibited from operating a vessel or registering a vessel for a one-year period; if they own the vessel, registration and tags are impounded for one year.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Upon the approach of a law enforcement vessel displaying a blue flashing light, what must the operator of any vessel do?
choice_a: Speed up to clear the area quickly
choice_b: Continue on course unless directly hailed
choice_c: Stop or give way in any situation until the law enforcement vessel has passed
choice_d: Turn off all navigation lights
explanation: The operator of any vessel shall stop or give-way in any situation until the law enforcement vessel with a blue flashing light has passed.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: No person shall create a wake within how many feet of a stopped law enforcement vessel displaying a blue flashing light?
choice_c: 300 feet
choice_d: 100 feet
explanation: No person shall operate a vessel that creates a wake within 100 feet of a stopped law enforcement vessel with a blue flashing light.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: A person participating in towed water sports must generally confine that activity to what area?
choice_a: A designated ski zone or open zone
choice_b: Any open area of the lake
choice_c: Within 100 feet of shore only
choice_d: Wherever traffic is lightest at the time
explanation: Any person participating in towed water sports must confine that activity within a designated ski zone or open zone.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: A vessel towing a water skier must have an observer aboard who meets what minimum requirement?
choice_c: A licensed boat operator
choice_d: No observer is required if the operator has a rearview mirror
explanation: Any person towing a skier must have an observer 10 years of age or older in the vessel who observes the person being towed at all times.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Water skiing after dark is prohibited except under what circumstance?
choice_a: It is never permitted under any circumstance
choice_b: If the skier wears a reflective vest
choice_c: Upon special permit
choice_d: If the towing vessel displays extra navigation lights
explanation: No person shall water ski or be towed between sunset and sunrise except upon special permit.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Why does the guide specifically warn against bow riding?
choice_b: It is only dangerous on Lake Erie
choice_c: It violates the vessel's capacity plate rating
choice_d: Unexpected movement, waves, or a sudden course change could throw the passenger into the water, risking being run over or struck by the propeller
explanation: Bow riding is especially dangerous because unexpected movement, large waves, or a sudden change in course could throw the passenger overboard, risking injury from being run over or struck by the propeller.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: What must a vessel operator NOT do regarding the information on a capacity plate?
choice_a: Alter, remove or deface any information on the plate
choice_c: Compare it to the boat's registration
choice_d: Show it to a law enforcement officer upon request
explanation: No person shall alter, remove or deface any information on the capacity plate.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: If a watercraft has no capacity plate, when is operation still prohibited?
choice_a: Operation is always allowed without a plate
choice_b: If a reasonably prudent person would believe the total load or horsepower presents a risk of physical harm
choice_c: Only if the vessel is over 40 feet long
choice_d: Only on Lake Erie
explanation: When no capacity plate exists, operation is prohibited if a reasonably prudent person would believe the total load or horsepower presents a risk of physical harm to persons or property.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Which agencies/officers are listed as having authority to enforce Ohio's watercraft laws?
choice_c: Sheriffs, municipal police, wildlife officers, and park or conservancy district officers, among others
choice_d: Only U.S. Coast Guard officers
explanation: Sheriffs, deputy sheriffs, marshals, municipal police officers, township police constables, wildlife officers, park or conservancy district officers, and other law enforcement officers may enforce state watercraft laws.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Except for persons legally hunting, when is discharging a firearm while in or on a vessel permitted?
choice_a: It is always permitted if the person has a concealed carry license
choice_b: It is permitted at any time on Lake Erie
choice_c: It is permitted for target practice with prior notice to the Division
choice_d: It is never permitted, with the sole exception of legal hunting
explanation: Except for persons legally engaged in hunting, no person shall discharge a firearm while in or on a vessel.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: An operator involved in a vessel collision or accident must do what, to the extent possible without risking serious danger?
choice_a: Render assistance as may be practicable and necessary
choice_b: Leave the scene immediately to avoid liability
choice_c: Wait for a law enforcement officer to arrive before taking any action
choice_d: Contact their insurance company before doing anything else
explanation: The operator of a vessel involved in a collision or accident shall render assistance as may be practicable and necessary, to the extent possible without risking serious danger to their own vessel, crew and passengers.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: A vessel accident must be reported on a full, prescribed form if it results in which of the following?
choice_a: Any damage at all, even a single scratch
choice_c: Only if a fatality occurs
choice_d: Only if the vessel is a personal watercraft
explanation: A full report must be filed if the accident results in loss of life, disappearance of an occupant, injury requiring medical treatment beyond first aid, property damage in excess of $1,000, or complete loss of a vessel.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: What is the quickest way to report a boating accident from a mobile phone, per the guide?
choice_c: Dial #ODNR
choice_d: Email the local sheriff's office
explanation: To report a boating accident, dial #ODNR.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Under Ohio law, what legal effect does a watercraft law violation have if it results in injury to a person or damage to property?
choice_a: It is automatically dismissed as an accident
choice_b: It has no bearing on any civil case
choice_c: It is treated only as a parking-style infraction
choice_d: It constitutes prima-facie evidence of negligence in a civil action
explanation: Violations of watercraft law that result in injury to persons or damage to property shall constitute prima-facie evidence of negligence in a civil action.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: What is the ODNR's designated "Powerboat Safety Month," with an emphasis on carbon monoxide dangers?
choice_c: August
choice_d: October
explanation: April is designated "Powerboat Safety Month" with an emphasis on the dangers of carbon monoxide.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Which of the following can increase the risk of carbon monoxide buildup aboard a boat, per the guide?
choice_a: Traveling at high speed in open water
choice_b: Traveling at slow speeds or idling, and a tail wind blowing exhaust toward passengers
choice_c: Using a marine CO detector
choice_d: Seating children in the forward-most seating
explanation: Traveling at slow speeds or idling can cause carbon monoxide to build up on the boat; a tail wind may blow exhaust toward passengers.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning aboard a boat can mirror what other common condition, per the guide?
choice_c: Seasickness
choice_d: Hypothermia
explanation: Symptoms of CO poisoning mirror seasickness.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Ohio State Park boating regulations under OAC 1501:47-3 apply to which waters?
choice_c: Only privately owned marinas
choice_d: Only lakes at Ohio State Parks
explanation: The State Park boating rules apply only to lakes at Ohio State Parks.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: From sunset to sunrise, what is the speed limit for all Ohio State Park lakes within designated speed zones, ski zones, or open zones?
choice_c: 15 miles per hour
choice_d: 25 miles per hour
explanation: From sunset to sunrise, the speed limit for all Ohio State Park lakes is 10 miles per hour in designated speed zones, ski zones, or open zones.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: What is prohibited while being towed by a watercraft on Ohio State Park waters, per the airfoil rule?
choice_b: Having any airfoil or balloon for the purpose of becoming airborne
choice_c: Using a rope longer than 50 feet
choice_d: Towing more than one person at a time
explanation: While being towed, no person shall have any airfoil or balloon for the purpose of becoming airborne over Ohio State Park waters.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Air propelled powercraft and hovercraft are prohibited on Ohio State Park waters, EXCEPT in the speed or ski zone at which named lakes?
choice_c: Indian Lake, Grand Lake St. Marys, Buckeye Lake, Mosquito Lake, Rocky Fork Lake, and Lake Milton
choice_d: They are banned everywhere in Ohio without exception
explanation: Air propelled powercraft or hovercraft are permitted only in the speed or ski zone (and the water leading directly from a ramp or dock to those zones) at Indian Lake, Grand Lake St. Marys, Buckeye Lake, Mosquito Lake, Rocky Fork Lake, and Lake Milton.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: On Ohio State Park waters, sleeping aboard a vessel at night is prohibited EXCEPT where?
choice_a: Anywhere the vessel is anchored more than 100 feet from shore
choice_b: It is prohibited under all circumstances, with no exceptions
choice_c: Only on vessels over 26 feet in length
choice_d: In designated boat camping/sleeping locations
explanation: No boat operator shall sleep at night aboard a vessel on Ohio State Park waters except in designated locations.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: Swimming, bathing, diving or wading from a watercraft on Ohio State Park water is prohibited EXCEPT where?
choice_a: In officially designated boat swimming areas
choice_c: It is completely prohibited with no exceptions
choice_d: Only from vessels under 20 feet long
explanation: No person shall swim, bathe, dive, or wade from any watercraft in Ohio State Park water except in officially designated boat swimming areas.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: What is prohibited regarding alcohol on watercraft on waters administered by Ohio State Parks?
choice_a: Bringing any food or beverage aboard
choice_b: Overtly and publicly consuming or displaying beer or intoxicating liquor
choice_c: Only glass containers are prohibited
choice_d: Alcohol is fully permitted with no restriction at all
explanation: No person shall overtly and publicly consume or display the presence of any beer or intoxicating liquor on any watercraft on waters administered by Ohio State Parks.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: No person shall operate a powercraft within or through a Ohio State Park shore zone, danger zone, or marked no-wake area in what manner?
choice_c: At a speed that produces a wake
choice_d: With a valid registration on board
explanation: No person shall operate a powercraft within or through a shore zone, danger zone or any area marked as a no wake zone at a speed that produces a wake.

topic: Ohio Operating Laws, Vessel Accidents & State Parks Regulations
question: No person shall operate a vessel without sufficient control to avoid an incident resulting in which of the following, per Ohio's "Failure to Control" law?
choice_a: A late return to the marina
choice_c: Running out of fuel
choice_d: Property damage, physical injury, or loss of life
explanation: No person shall operate a vessel without sufficient control to avoid an incident that results in property damage, physical injury, loss of life, or any combination of these.
